A1.evidence: The scripts are retrievable over HTTPS via the article landing page (Row 6 entitlement). The paper states 'Data and materials are available in the Supplement' (l. 566).

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS via the article landing page is an open, free, universally implementable protocol.

A1_2.evidence: No access control is stated or warranted for the analysis scripts. Open access needing no authentication satisfies A1.2 (v2.1).

A2.evidence: Row 6: no independent metadata record, so A2 = 0 for the supplement-only code.

F1.evidence: The paper's own analysis code (the revised OxCal model, l. 267, and the 'ArchaeoPhases code to reproduce the figure', Figs 3-4 captions) is in the publisher Supplement under the article DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2023.105765. A supplement under the article DOI scores F1 = 1 (v2.1).

F2.evidence: Row 6 supplement-only deposit: no independent metadata record. No code repository, CodeMeta, or CITATION.cff is cited.

F3.evidence: Row 6: no resource-level metadata record carrying an identifier for the scripts.

F4.evidence: Row 6: the scripts are not indexed in any registry. The ArchaeoPhases CRAN listing is a third-party dependency and never substitutes for the paper's own scripts.

I1.evidence: The code is written in standard, openly documented languages: an OxCal (CQL) model ('implemented in OxCal', l. 267) and R code using ArchaeoPhases ('the R code for tempo and occurrence plots', Author's Contributions, ll. 560-561).

I2.evidence: No vocabulary or ontology standards for the software or its metadata are evidenced.

I3.evidence: Dependency citations: 'functions provided by ArchaeoPhases software (Philippe & Vibet, 2020)' (l. 529), whose reference carries DOI 10.18637/jss.v093.c01 (printed with a doubled resolver prefix, 'https://doi.org/https://doi.org/...'); and 'OxCal version 4.4.2' with Bronk Ramsey (2001, 2009). The qualified, PID-bearing reference holds for the principal dependency. The pack's CRAN record is endpoint-flagged and does not resolve, so it adds nothing.

R1.evidence: The paper describes the code richly: the model structure ('two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences', ll. 268-270), the MCMC tallying algorithm ('The depositional histories of each pair of beads is observed at each iteration of the MCMC output and a tally kept...', ll. 331-336), and the purpose of each script (Figs 3-4 captions; branching probabilities 'see Supplement').

R1_1.evidence: No code licence is stated. The publisher-hosted supplement defaults to the article's licence. The publisher Crossref record carries only Elsevier TDM/user-licence and 10.15223 policy URLs, with no open licence, and these are more restrictive than the CC-BY-NC-ND on the White Rose accepted-version cover, so the most-restrictive rule gives no clear usage licence. ArchaeoPhases' CRAN licence belongs to a third-party dependency and cannot substitute.

R1_2.evidence: Code provenance is documented. Authorship: 'AP maintains the ArchaeoPhases software, improved the R code for tempo and occurrence plots'; 'TSD drafted ... the supplementary material'. Advice on OxCal code is acknowledged (Millard, Bronk Ramsey, et al.). Software version: OxCal 4.4.2 with IntCal20. The model derives from the Bayliss et al. (2013) prior with documented modifications, and five independent runs are reported.

R1_3.evidence: The paper's own scripts show no package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or community review. ArchaeoPhases being on CRAN is third-party and never substitutes (aggregation rule), and the pack's CRAN record is endpoint-flagged (unresolved gap).

A1.evidence: Coverage is substantial (4/5 datasets Tier 0-2, 80%), so the A1 completeness override does not apply. The principal Supplement is retrievable over HTTPS via the article landing page (Row 6 entitlement), and the upstream ADS archive resolves by DOI (pack DataCite record, http_status 200).

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS delivery via the article landing page (Row 6) and DOI/HTTPS resolution for ADS. These protocols are open, free, and universally implementable. The paper states no proprietary access mechanism.

A1_2.evidence: No access control is stated, and none is warranted: the data are archaeological radiocarbon, grave, and bead-occurrence data with no ethical or CARE sensitivity. The paper says simply 'Data and materials are available in the Supplement'. A fully open resource needing no authentication satisfies A1.2 (v2.1).

A2.evidence: Row 6: a supplement-only deposit has no independent metadata record, so A2 = 0. Article-level Crossref persistence is not resource-level metadata persistence.

F1.evidence: Principal dataset is the publisher Supplement ('Data and materials are available in the Supplement', l. 566; revised OxCal model with likelihoods and occurrences, ll. 267-270), distributed under the article DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2023.105765. Under the v2.1 F1 rule, a supplement under the article DOI scores 1. The pack's Crossref record is declared by both the article and the supplement.

F2.evidence: Supplement-only deposit with no independent deposit named in the paper. Platform Row 6 applies: no independent metadata record, so F2 = 0. The upstream ADS archive is non-principal because the revised model in the Supplement supersedes it for reproduction, and conjunctive scoring would fail on the Supplement anyway.

F3.evidence: Row 6: no independent metadata record carrying a resource-level identifier, so F3 = 0. Crossref 'identifier_in_metadata: true' describes the article record, not the supplement.

F4.evidence: Row 6: no registry indexing of the supplement as a resource, so F4 = 0.

I1.evidence: The data are embedded in a tool-specific OxCal model script ('It comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types', ll. 268-270). No shared structured data representation (CSV with schema, JSON, XML) is documented, the supplement's file format is not stated, and no pack record speaks to it.

I2.evidence: Bead types use the Brugmann (2004) and Nielsen (2013) typology codes (e.g. BE1-CylRound, BE3-Amber), an ad hoc published classification with no PIDs or machine-readable vocabulary. No FAIR vocabulary (PeriodO, AAT, etc.) is cited.

I3.evidence: The paper states a typed derivation relation to a PID-identified upstream dataset: 'Chronological relations among the female graves are based on a chronological prior from the OxCal model deposited in the project archive (Hines, 2013)' (ll. 232-234). The reference gives 'https://doi.org/10.5284/1018290', which the pack confirms as a findable DataCite dataset record.

R1.evidence: The paper describes the dataset richly: 72 female graves (52 from Hines & Bayliss 2013, 20 from RAF Lakenheath, Hines 2021; ll. 212-219), a model with likelihoods/constraints and occurrences for each bead type (ll. 268-270), 23 bead types (Fig. 4), and which stratigraphic and known-age constraints were retained or removed, with reasons (ll. 236-260).

R1_1.evidence: No separate supplement licence is stated, so per R1.1(a) the supplement takes the article's licence. Sources disagree for the article: the White Rose accepted-version cover says CC-BY-NC-ND, while the publisher Crossref record lists only Elsevier TDM/user-licence URLs and 10.15223 policy identifiers, with no open content licence. The more restrictive publisher terms govern, effectively all rights reserved, so no clear data usage licence applies to the publisher-hosted supplement.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is documented. Sources: Hines & Bayliss 2013, Hines 2021, and the ADS-deposited project OxCal model. Transformations: three named constraints removed, with justification, and stratigraphic/artefact constraints retained (ll. 247-260). Processing: 'calibrates with OxCal version 4.4.2 and the IntCal20 calibration curve'; 'five independent runs of the model indicate negligible between-run variability' (ll. 270-273).

R1_3.evidence: Supplement-only deposit: no deposit-level metadata schema or domain repository applies. OxCal and IntCal20 are methodological standards and do not qualify under v2.1 R1.3. ADS (route c) holds only the non-principal upstream archive, and conjunctive scoring fails on the Supplement.
